before.card: A chemigram creates an image by manipulating photographic paper with chemicals and substances that resist them. Working in full light lets materials such as oils or varnishes shape the reaction. Chance and direct intervention can both influence marks without a camera recording an external scene.

evidence.note: Chemical manipulation, resists, full light and experimental chance are described.

before.label: Chemigram
before.learning_takeaway: Chemigrams manipulate photosensitive paper with resists and photographic chemicals in full light, allowing chemical interaction and chance to shape the image.

relations.note: Compare a chemical-resist image with an object-shadow image made through light exposure.

after.card: A chemigram creates an image by manipulating photographic paper with chemicals, often using oils or varnishes. Working in full light combines the maker’s intervention with chance. The marks emerge from material reactions without a camera recording an external scene.

evidence.note: The V&A describes direct chemical manipulation of photographic paper, often using oils or varnishes, in full light with chance; its Photogram entry supports the contrasting exposure process.
